sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Cohesive Forces**: Molecules deep inside a liquid experience equal attractive forces from all directions, whereas surface molecules experience a net inward **inward pull** due to unbalanced intermolecular forces.
• **Surface Energy**: The potential energy per unit area of the surface; work done in stretching the surface area by a unit amount is stored as **surface energy** ($W = \sigma \Delta A$).
• **Temperature Dependence**: Surface tension **decreases with an increase in temperature** because increased thermal kinetic energy weakens the intermolecular cohesive bonds.
• **Effect of Impurities**: Soluble impurities like soap or detergents drastically **reduce surface tension** by breaking cohesive hydrogen bonds between water molecules.

items.definition: Cohesion is attraction between identical molecules (water-water); adhesion is attraction between dissimilar molecules (water-glass).
The angle formed by the liquid-solid interface inside the liquid; acute for wetting liquids (water-glass) and obtuse for non-wetting liquids (mercury-glass).
Pressure difference between inside and outside of a curved liquid surface; $P = 2\sigma/r$ for a liquid drop and $P = 4\sigma/r$ for a soap bubble.
Irregular dissolution of camphor reduces local surface tension, causing rapid erratic movements on water surfaces.

items.title: Major Physiological & Environmental Applications
items.content:
• **Stomata and Plant Xylem**: Water transport against gravity relies on cohesive tension of water columns in xylem vessels.
• **Respiratory System**: Pulmonary surfactant reduces surface tension in alveoli, preventing lung collapse during exhalation.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Environmental Impact**: Oil spills spread over oceans form thin films; adding dispersants alters surface tension to break up slicks.
• **Industrial Optimization**: Controlling surface tension is critical in nano-coatings, inkjet printing, and agrochemical spraying efficiency.

items.title: Mnemonic for Excess Pressure Formula ($2\sigma/r$ vs $4\sigma/r$)
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "Drop has ONE surface, Bubble has TWO surfaces (inner and outer)."
• **Decoded Meaning**: Drop = $2\sigma/r$, Bubble = $4\sigma/r$.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly eliminates confusion in numerical or direct formula-based matching questions.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Soap lowers surface tension; Heat kills surface tension; Impurities drop tension.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often states that 'surface tension increases with temperature.' Remember that surface tension *decreases* as temperature rises because thermal energy overcomes intermolecular attraction.
Mains Value Addition: Link surface tension concepts to nanotechnology (superhydrophobic lotus leaf effect / biomimicry) and public health (pulmonary surfactant deficiencies in premature infants).

keyTakeaways: Surface tension arises from unbalanced inward cohesive forces on liquid surface molecules, minimizing surface area.
Temperature increase and detergent addition both decrease surface tension by disrupting intermolecular bonds.
Capillary action and excess pressure formulas ($2\sigma/r$ vs $4\sigma/r$) are highest-yield areas for Prelims MCQs.
